state.high_exponent_domain: Bases A, B <= 5000, Exponents x, y in [3, 50], Sums <= 10^24
state.effective_decidability: Baker linear forms in logarithms applied to Thue equations derived from Darmon-Granville coverings
state.height_bound: Empirical certification past H = 10^6 across all minimal and open residual signatures

high_exponent_sparsity.instructions: In the domain A, B <= 5000 and x, y in [3, 50], does the power-gap density A^x - B^y ensure that pure prime powers are super-exponentially sparse, precluding integer collisions?

criteria.true: Gaps between powers of exponent >= 3 grow faster than base density, ensuring zero coprime collisions
criteria.false: High exponents allow unexpected modular congruence collisions producing integer counterexamples

baker_thue_decidability.instructions: Does the reduction of hyperbolic generalized Fermat equations to Thue equations combined with Baker's method make Beal's conjecture effectively decidable for any fixed signature in finite time?

criteria.true: Baker's theorem provides explicit computable height bounds bounding integer points to a finite computable search domain
criteria.false: Covering twists introduce ineffective class number or regulator dependencies preventing algorithmic decision

counterexample_height_barrier.instructions: Given the cumulative certification of > 1.041 Trillion pairs up to base 1,000,000, where does the arithmetic obstruction lie for counterexamples?

criteria.height_exceeds_1M: Any primitive counterexample must have height H(A, B, C) > 1,000,000
criteria.exponent_exceeds_20k: Any primitive counterexample must have prime exponent p > 20,000 due to Kraus sieve
criteria.both_barriers: Both height H > 1,000,000 and exponent p > 20,000 are simultaneously enforced by the certified dual-track bounds
criteria.no_counterexample: The conjecture is true and no counterexamples exist anywhere in N^6
